pull.title: mining: add Block interface, fix template data race
pull.body:
This PR catches two birds with one stone:

- fixes https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/issues/36515
- adds a `Block` interface, which lets IPC clients fetch the block data (or its header)

This means a client can still fetch (and store) the block after `submitSolution()`, but we no longer mutate the template's `CBlock` for this.

### Block interface

`submitSolution()` no longer modifies the template. It applies the solution to a copy of the template block and returns a `Block` handle for that copy, also when the block is rejected.

`Mining::submitBlock()` and `BlockTemplate::block()` do the same. The new interface has a `data()`, `header()` and `coinbaseMerklePath()` method, so these are migrated from the `BlockTemplate` interface.

The interface can be expanded later, e.g. to tell whether the block is part of the active chain (or went stale, useful for a miner to know).

This is a breaking change for IPC clients:

- `getBlockHeader()` → `block().header()`
- `getBlock()` → `block().data()`
- `getCoinbaseMerklePath()` → `block().coinbaseMerklePath()`
- `bool submitSolution(..., reason, debug)` → `Block submitSolution(..., accepted, reason, debug)`
- `bool submitBlock(block, reason, debug)` → `Block submitBlock(block, accepted, reason, debug)`

It uses new ordinals and old methods throw.

`submitSolution()` now throws when the coinbase is null, instead of returning false.

### Performance

My agent measured how long after `submitSolution()` sv2-tp forwards the next template, with master as the baseline and an adapted sv2-tp as the client:

| Workload | Master | This PR | Paired median difference (95% CI) |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Empty block | 1.32 ms | 1.40 ms | +0.05 ms [−0.11, +0.15] |
| Near-full block, 3.7 MB | 10.11 ms | 10.07 ms | −0.09 ms [−0.44, +0.28] |

The extra `block()` call costs about 0.15 ms per template for a C++ client. The alternative approach of having `submitSolution()` return the full `CBlock` added 6ms.

The vector was initially introduced for (internal) compatibility with the `getblocktemplate` RPC, which returns this fee information.

`sv2-tp` only uses fees (the total) for logging, the SRI implementation doesn't use it at all.

I haven't done an inventory of software out there that uses the fees from `getblocktemplate`. One use case I could imagine is a miner dashboard that shows the current template you're working on, and a breakdown of fees.

We definitely need the internal total. Providing the total and individual via IPC is trivial, so I think we should keep it.

> See minimal test that fails on our tsan functional tests.

It works and I'm open to taking it, but failure isn't deterministic (just very likely with the 100 iterations).
Concept ACK

ACK 4774cf1de6a4670323686bf93beb93035b3f6dad

This change fixes a data race between ipc calls running on different worker threads, where `submitSolution` modifies a template while another call reads it. It also adds the `getTotalFees` IPC method, allowing external clients to retrieve the total fees without summing individual transaction fees.

Ran @ismaelsadeeq’s ipc test with tsan, repeating each submission setting (100, 150, 200 and 300) 25 times. Without the mutex fix, every run detected the race. With the fix, every run passed with no race reports or timeouts

I think the test is worth including. even though reproduction depends on scheduling, it consistently caught the regression on my machine (macOS arm)

Added the test in a new commit, with some adjustments:
- use `timeout_factor` to avoid false positive failures
- improve cleanup

Might it be preferable to make `m_block_template` non-mutating? Do users of the interface even need the mutated template after submitting?
AFAICT no, so we could do that and make the template const, that way no race and we copy when mutating for submission.

> Might it be preferable to make m_block_template non-mutating? 

I think it's a preferable solution. With no writes after construction there's no race, and since `submitSolution()` already copies the block, calling `AddMerkleRootAndCoinbase()` on that copy instead of on the template costs nothing.

The documentation and tests would need to be updated too, since the in-place mutation is documented and tested since #33745 (released in v31).

The sv2-tp client apparently relies on that mutation (`SaveBlockAsync()`), but it may be easy to update.

> Do users of the interface even need the mutated template after submitting?

Yes. Both existing clients call `getBlock()` after submit to store a copy of the block. This is potentially very useful when debugging a rejected block.

> The sv2-tp client apparently relies on that mutation (`SaveBlockAsync()`), but it may be easy to update.

Clients could download the non-mutated block and re-apply the solution themselves before storing to disk. That's slightly more complicated, so I prefer the existing approach.
Could we just return the block copy after applying the solution?

@ismaelsadeeq in theory yes, but clients intentionally wait 1 second before requesting it. If the solution _is_ correct, we don't want to "distract" the node from relaying it and from producing the next template.

> If the solution is correct, we don't want to "distract" the node from relaying it and from producing the next template.

I don't understand what you mean here. Doesn't the new valid header get processed synchronously anyway?

A call to `getBlock()` locks `cs_main` (briefly). Since `sv2-tp` typically runs on the same machine, when it saves to disk it also blocks the OS. Creating the new template blocks `cs_main`. And IIUC so does our p2p code when it announces the new block and handles compact block missing-transaction requests.

That said, I haven't done a very thorough analysis on whether the 1 second delay before `getBlock()` actually matters.

> A call to getBlock() locks cs_main (briefly). Since sv2-tp typically runs on the same machine, when it saves to disk it also blocks the OS. Creating the new template blocks cs_main. And IIUC so does our p2p code when it announces the new block and handles compact block missing-transaction requests.

That should all be unrelated to copying a block. Or is the concern just that the OS might be something more important in the meantime and this might distract it? I don't think that is a valid concern.

I wrote:

> A call to `getBlock()` locks `cs_main` (briefly).

This is not the case.

I benchmarked the approach of making the template block immutable and returning the full block in `submitSolution()`. The good news is that there's no regression in compact block relay, not even when a transaction is missing.

But it does add a 6ms slowdown to when sv2-tp serves the next template. That's because IPC code still bottlenecks a few things on a single thread (even with multiple connections).

I was able to reduce that by having sv2-tp skip block deserialization (including sha256 hashing), and write the serialized bytes straight to disk (after a 500ms delay). That still left 2.5ms.

Things can be sped up further by:
1. having another thread copy the result (1ms) 
2. taking advantage of Capnp shared memory support: https://capnproto.org/cxxrpc.html (1ms)
3. more fundamentally making IPC (response) handling parallel

These require changes to libmultiprocess.

So my preference would be to defer making CBlockTemplate const until after these improvements land. This would be a breaking change for clients, but that's straight-forward to work around.

There's another approach, though a bit of a layer violation: we can have `submitSolution()` defer its response so it comes _after_ `waitNext()`. But I also prefer doing that as a followup, rather than increase the scope of this PR.
Rebased after #36192.

One of the selling points of Stratum v2 is lower latency, see e.g. https://stratumprotocol.org/blog/case-study/hashlabs/

> SV2 with Job Declaration reduces block propagation time from 96.3 milliseconds (SV1) to just 3.44 milliseconds, making block propagation faster.

I don't know what methodology they used (might be a bit optimistic), but adding 6ms just for a code style improvement, doesn't seem justified in light of those numbers.

Thanks @Sjors! I was able to reproduce it on my machine. I got similar results.

The latency measured doens't affect block propagation but "Block Change latency" which is 325 ms for SV1 and 1.42 ms for SV2 with JD. I still consider the 6ms after `submitSolution` a negligible delay because its average cost per network block is about 6 ms × hashrate share: ~1.8 ms for a 30% pool, ~0.06 ms for a 1% miner.

That said, I don’t feel strongly about. I am fine with it being a future follow up.

test: exercise concurrent IPC block template access

Read a template while submitting solutions through a separate IPC worker
thread to cover races between the getters and submitSolution(), and
check that the template header and block never change. Repeat
submissions to increase the chance of detecting a race under
ThreadSanitizer.

Bound the scenario and template cleanup using timeout_factor, and cancel
and await both concurrent tasks before destroying the template.

Co-authored-by: Abubakar Sadiq Ismail <48946461+ismaelsadeeq@users.noreply.github.com>

events.body:
I added a new `Block` interface. To keep this PR simple, I'm going to open a fresh PR for `getTotalFees()`, since it no longer makes sense to combine that feature (requested in https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35671#issuecomment-6165435275) with the fix for https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/issues/36515. Most review on this PR was focussed on the latter.

The `Block` interface is returned by `submitSolution()`, `submitBlock()` and `getBlock()`. It starts out with just `data()`, `header()` and `coinbaseMerklePath()`. The latter two are moved out of `BlockTemplate`.

It could later be expanded later to e.g. say if a block is part of the active chain (very useful for a miner to know).

The `coinbaseTx()` getter stays on the template, because it does not return the actual coinbase transaction but rather a struct that is only useful for mining software to _generate_ a coinbase transaction. 

I'm keeping `getTxFees()` and `getTxSigops()` in the template, because they are calculated at template generation time and non-trivial to calculate in other contexts.

The chain interface proposed in #29409 might also be able to use this.

I renamed `getBlock()` to `block()`, so clients call `block().data()` to get the block's data. Note that this takes advantage of Cap’n Proto promise pipelining (see the `ipc_util.py` change).

This is a breaking change and I intentionally made `getBlockOld2`, etc fail, because in the past reviewers complained when I made backward compatible changes while the interface is still experimental. This is no problem for sv2-tp and SRI which are pretty good at handling our breaking changes between our major releases. (FWIW my goal is to remove the experimental status after Windows support lands)

I ran the performance benchmark again and there's no regression, so: a better interface, no need for a mutex and it stays fast.

Code review 1f9fcfab45fa2bdd8296c265dfac2dd206a353bc

The approach is sound to me, but now the `Block` capability served to clients holds references to TXs that might leave the mempool. IPC clients now take responsibility for dropping these block capabilities and as a result freeing up memory on the node (good this is that this is trivial to inspect with the `getMemoryLoad` method proposed in #33922). This behaviour change should be documented in the PR description and the first commit msg.

Planning to review more.

mining: return Block from submitSolution(), keep template unchanged

submitSolution() applies the solution to a copy of the template block
instead of modifying the template. It returns a handle to that copy,
also when the block is rejected, and reports acceptance through a new
accepted output. A null coinbase now throws instead of returning false.

The template no longer changes after creation, so IPC calls on
different worker threads can't race when one of them submits a solution.

In mining.capnp the new signature takes a new ordinal, @12. The old
ordinal, @10, becomes submitSolutionOld10, a deprecated stub that
returns an error.

Fixes #36515.

mining: add Block interface, return it from BlockTemplate::block()

Add interfaces::Block, a handle to a block whose data() method returns
the full block. BlockTemplate::block() returns such a handle and
replaces getBlock().

In mining.capnp block() takes a new ordinal, @11. The old ordinal, @2,
becomes getBlockOld2, a deprecated stub that returns an error.

The handle shares the block with its template, so it reflects
modifications made by submitSolution(). A later commit will stop
submitSolution() from modifying the template.

A Block handle keeps the template's memory, including its transactions,
allocated until the client destroys the handle.

Co-authored-by: ViniciusCestarii <viniciuscestari01@gmail.com>
